items.title: Trump weighs Iran options after first post-election security meeting
items.summary: Trump met top national security advisers on 5 Nov to discuss Iran, RBC-Ukraine reports, with war or de-escalation possible within days. Gulf and regional mediators are pushing a plan in which the US lifts its naval blockade and unfreezes some assets in return for IAEA inspections and a reopened Strait of Hormuz. Details are provisional.
items.why: A war-or-deal decision moves oil, inflation and corporate budgets, and with them hiring plans in India.

items.title: Report: US considering resuming strikes on Iran from 9 November
items.summary: TASS, citing Fox News, says Washington is weighing a renewed military operation against Iran as early as Monday 9 November. This is a single relayed report and could not be confirmed elsewhere, so treat it as provisional.
items.why: Escalation risk keeps energy prices and markets volatile, a backdrop for every business case this term.

items.title: What a Democratic Congress means for Iran and Ukraine policy
items.summary: CNBC analysts say Democratic control of Congress after the midterms is likely to bring tougher oversight of the administration's handling of Iran and Ukraine. Rubio has cast doubt on a quick Ukraine deal, while Trump pushes for talks.
items.why: Policy gridlock or oversight in Washington shapes sanctions, trade rules and the outlook for global firms.

items.title: Austria's chancellor visits China as APEC leaders' meeting nears
items.summary: Austrian Chancellor Christian Stocker is in China from 2 to 7 November for the China International Import Expo and talks with President Xi Jinping. The APEC CEO Summit follows in Shenzhen on 17 and 18 November, with the leaders' meeting later in the month (dates differ by source).
items.why: Europe-China engagement and APEC set the tone for trade, supply chains and market access in Asia.

items.title: Nifty reclaims 25,000 as the rally runs to a seventh day
items.summary: Business Standard reports the Nifty50 closed up 2.01% at 25,030.35 on 6 Nov, above 25,000 for the first time since February, with banks leading. It puts the Sensex at 81,028 after a gain of about 1,718 points; an intraday figure in the same outlet differs, so the Sensex close is provisional.
items.why: Strong markets support fundraising and tend to lift campus hiring sentiment in banking and consulting.

items.title: Opposition steps up call for the Chief Election Commissioner to resign
items.summary: Al Jazeera reports opposition parties renewed calls for Chief Election Commissioner Ganesh Kumar to resign after a large Delhi rally led by Rahul Gandhi and the INDIA bloc over voter-list revisions. The report is dated 3 November.
items.why: Political contests over institutions affect policy stability, which investors and employers watch closely.

items.title: Government doubles OMSS rice sale target to 50 lakh tonnes
items.summary: DD News reports the Centre doubled its Open Market Sale Scheme rice target to 50 lakh tonnes for 2026-27, with 25 lakh tonnes already sold through e-auctions.
items.why: Food price management feeds into inflation, real wages and consumer demand, key inputs for marketing plans.

items.title: India targets Rs 3 lakh crore of defence output by 2029
items.summary: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh said India aims for defence production worth Rs 3 lakh crore and defence exports of Rs 50,000 crore by 2029, according to the government news feed.
items.why: Defence manufacturing growth creates new hiring demand in engineering, operations and supply chain.

items.title: US added 165,000 jobs in October, well above forecasts
items.summary: TipRanks reports US payrolls rose 165,000 in October against a consensus near 70,000, with unemployment dipping to 4.1% and earlier months revised up. Forecasts quoted elsewhere were 59,000 to 65,000, so the size of the beat varies by source; the Dow slipped after the release.
items.why: A firm US labour market shapes interest-rate expectations and global hiring, including for Indian services firms.

items.title: Nasdaq tries to recover after its worst rout in 19 months
items.summary: CNBC's live coverage says the Nasdaq rebounded about 1.1% after Thursday's AI-led sell-off, when the S&P 500 fell 4.36% and the Nasdaq 5.52%. Airbnb and Cloudflare beat earnings estimates.
items.why: Swings in AI valuations change how fast firms invest in automation and the talent mix they hire.

items.title: Fox completes its roughly $22 billion purchase of Roku
items.summary: Fox Corp has closed its acquisition of streaming platform Roku, valued at about $22 billion, Fox Business reports. CEO Lachlan Murdoch pointed to Tubi as one of streaming's most successful businesses.
items.why: A big media-streaming consolidation is a live case in integration, culture and go-to-market strategy.

items.title: Kimberly-Clark completes its acquisition of Kenvue
items.summary: Kimberly-Clark has completed its acquisition of Kenvue, creating what it calls a global consumer health and wellness leader. CEO Mike Hsu called it a defining moment in the company's 154-year history. The deal closed on 2 November.
items.why: Post-merger integration of two consumer giants is a textbook HR and brand-portfolio challenge.

items.title: Analog Devices completes acquisition of Alif Semiconductor
items.summary: Analog Devices announced the completion of its acquisition of Alif Semiconductor, with CEO Vincent Roche welcoming the Alif team, according to its release.
items.why: Chip-sector consolidation continues despite market swings, shaping demand for semiconductor talent.

items.title: OpenAI reportedly raises $11 billion more at a $1.25 trillion valuation
items.summary: TechCrunch, citing Bloomberg, reports OpenAI has raised about $11 billion so far in a new round valuing it at $1.25 trillion. The same day, Bloomberg reported that buyers of Anthropic's planned IPO shares were eyeing a lower valuation than it targeted. Figures are as reported.
items.why: AI funding levels signal how aggressively firms will push AI into workplaces and HR tools.

items.title: Data-centre backlash hits AI companies after the US midterms
items.summary: Euronews reports AI stocks fell as voters and newly elected officials pushed back on data-centre construction; TSMC shares dropped about 10%. One roundup says voters rejected data centres in 40 of 41 local ballot measures on 3 Nov, and OpenAI offered to pay full power and grid costs at its sites.
items.why: Community and regulatory pushback is now a factor in where tech jobs and investment land.

items.title: Sentra raises $150 million as AI-security funding grows
items.summary: Cybersecurity firm Sentra raised a $150 million Series C led by Capital One Ventures to protect company data from unauthorised access by AI agents, leading a $233.5 million week for Africa and Middle East startups, Techloy reports.
items.why: Securing data from AI agents is a fast-growing area that shapes new roles and governance policies.

items.title: Seed investors pile into AI security start-ups
items.summary: Crunchbase News reports a rush of seed funding into cybersecurity start-ups built around AI, as investors bet on protecting companies adopting AI agents.
items.why: Where early money flows hints at the next wave of employers and skills in demand.

items.title: Nifty is back above 25,000 for the first time since February
items.summary: The Nifty50 closed at 25,030.35 on 6 Nov, its first close above 25,000 since 27 February 2026, as the rally ran to a seventh day.

items.title: US unemployment dipped to 4.1% in October
items.summary: October's jobs report showed 165,000 jobs added and unemployment down to 4.1%.

items.title: Voters rejected data centres in 40 of 41 local ballot measures
items.summary: An AI news roundup reports data centres lost 40 of 41 local ballot measures on 3 Nov, prompting OpenAI's offer to cover power and grid costs.
